trigger: run_off_lock() throws (e.g. std::bad_alloc constructing an Action/pair string key) after its probe_launches loop already launched a probe successfully in the same pass
independent_reporters: 3 of 3 (Kimi Phase 1, Codex Phase 2 independently re-derived, fjarvis + this session both independently re-verified against the code)
summary: unwind_pass_locked() skipped any probe_launches entry whose pl.job was already reset (i.e. actually launched), on the false assumption publish_locked()'s re-validation would still run for it - it does not, on exactly this throw-mid-pass path. Left the watch ProbeState::Pending with w.call==nullptr permanently: sweep_locked's Pending case is then a no-op forever, unrescuable by on_fire (Idle-only relaunch) or watch() (idempotent no-op on an already-watched key). Verified line-by-line against the code independently of fjarvis's report before accepting it (checked sweep_locked's Deferred->Pending promotion, run_off_lock's two-loop structure and its per-action try/catch scope, unwind_pass_locked's dispatched flag being set unconditionally before run_off_lock is even called, on_fire's Idle-only relaunch guard, and watch()'s idempotent-on-existing-key early return).
classification: judgment (reasoned from code read, independently re-verified, reproduced)
adjudicated_by: self (fork, independently re-verified fjarvis's finding before acting)
adjudication_rationale: Confirmed correct via direct code trace matching every step of the reported chain; fixed by extracting reconcile_probe_launches_locked() (shared, noexcept) and calling it unconditionally from unwind_pass_locked() instead of the old skip-only logic. Red-then-green regression test added (new emit_bookkeeping_hook test seam, fires only on a pass with a staged launch). RED verified on DGRHP at 515d43ed7 (probe_calls=2, strand_hook_consumed=1, delivered stayed 0 - CHECK failed as designed). GREEN verified at 96f03d589 (All tests passed, 8 assertions). Full Windows agent suite 53824 assertions/2767 cases clean at the fixed HEAD; targeted [walkoff]/[resilience]/[t6] subset 672 assertions/42 cases clean. Linux compile + agent suite (2 Ok/0 Fail) clean.

trigger: the Action string-key copy inside work.actions.push_back for a fault edge throws
summary: sweep_locked() flipped w.faulted_reported to match w.faulted_now BEFORE the Action push_back that stages the corresponding fault edge, whose own string-key copy can throw independently of the vector's (reserved) capacity. A throw there left faulted_reported wrongly pre-flipped with no Action ever recorded to later correct it. Fixed by reordering: stage first, flip after.
classification: judgment (reasoned from code read, independently re-verified)
adjudication_rationale: Simple, low-risk reorder matching the strong-exception-guarantee push_back already relied on elsewhere in this file. No dedicated regression test added (same allocation-failure class as ext1, effort budget prioritized ext1s test); exercised incidentally by the full suite's existing fault-edge coverage, which stays green.

trigger: a test raising drain_lane_cap above the compile-time kDrainLaneCap
summary: drain_outcomes_ is reserved to the compile-time kDrainLaneCap in start(), but run_off_lock() batches drain_launches against the runtime-overridable drain_lane_cap_. Verified: no test today sets drain_lane_cap above kDrainLaneCap (the one override in test_spark_mechanism.cpp sets it to 1, below the constant) - test-seam-only, dormant today. Not fixed; documented in place instead (a future test raising the cap would need the reserve raised to match).
adjudication_rationale: LOW, no live trigger exists in the test suite today; a code comment records the invariant so a future test that raises the cap does not silently reintroduce the mismatch. Not worth the same-pass risk of touching start()'s reserve sizing for a scenario nothing currently exercises.

trigger: run_off_lock() throws after dispatched=true with entries already recorded in work.succeeded_emits/failed_emits earlier in the same pass
independent_reporters: 1 of 1 (fjarvis, as part of the fault-edge finding's second half)
summary: unwind_pass_locked()'s if (!dispatched) guard still skips succeeded_emits/failed_emits reconciliation whenever dispatched=true (i.e. whenever run_off_lock() was entered at all, which is unconditionally true per ext1's finding) - unlike probe_launches, which ext1's fix made unconditional. A degraded-but-not-catastrophic gap: a legitimate emit success's retry-count reset, or a legitimate failure's resync-debt restoration, from earlier in the same pass is silently dropped if something later in the pass throws. NOT extended to be unconditional in this fix round: publish_locked's failed_emits path calls spdlog::warn(), and moving that into a shared noexcept helper needs a deliberate decision on whether a formatting/allocation failure inside logging is acceptable to std::terminate() on.
adjudication_rationale: Filed as GitHub issue #4229 (bundled with the health-grace-boundary-miss finding) rather than fixed in this already-large round - degrades retry bookkeeping for one pass, does not strand a watch permanently (distinguishing it from ext1), and the noexcept-vs-logging design question deserves its own scoped review.

trigger: a probe's try_take() succeeds on the exact sweep pass that would otherwise have called grace_check_locked() for it
summary: grace_check_locked() is called only from sweep_locked's Pending/Deferred NOT-ready branches; a probe that resolves successfully on the same pass that would have flagged it as past-grace skips the grace check entirely, committing as if it had always been healthy - no Faulted-then-Recovered pair on the wire, contrary to D12's duration-based contract. Observability-only (no data loss, no stuck state).
classification: judgment (reasoned from code read, independently re-verified)
adjudication_rationale: Filed as GitHub issue #4229 alongside ext4 - observability-only, no operator-visible correctness impact, deserves its own design pass rather than a rushed same-pass fix.
